newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to offer more short-term bills.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to offer more short-term bills.

text.p: The Philippine Bureau of Treasury said on Thursday it had decided to offer more short-term bills next week because of the prevailing high interest rates.
Treasury director Roberto Juanchito Dispo said the government would cut the Treasury bill offer next week to 2.5 billion pesos from 5.0 billion pesos.

It would also defer Tuesday's scheduled offer of 3.5 billion pesos worth of seven-year, fixed-rate T-bonds and instead offer 35-day and 42-day cash management bills in the amount of three billion pesos each.
Dispo said the total offers for next week will still remain at 8.5 billion pesos.
"Why borrow long when interest rates are high? Intelligence dictates that we should borrow short," he said.
For the T-bill offer on Monday, he said one billion pesos each of 91-day and 182-day bills would be sold and 500 million pesos of 364-day bills would be offered.
Previously, the government sold the 91-day and 182-day bills at a weekly volume of 1.5 billion pesos each and the 364-day bills in the volume of two billion pesos.
Dispo said the government would still have to decide whether this new composition of bills would be implemented after next week.
This would depend on whether the market stabilises, he said.
T-bill rates rose to a two-year high this week following the volatility in the currency market caused by the de facto devaluation of the Philippine peso and the Thai baht.
